messages:
maria: quick heads-up — on canary 0.3.4 I noticed small but consistent numeric diffs between fused-qkv + bias+rope fusion + dropout-free path vs the legacy path. Not huge (1e-3-ish) but causes a couple of our eval slices to flip.
kevin: thanks for flagging. do you have a minimal repro? is this fp16 accumulation noise or an actual ordering bug?
aj: can you paste the failing example? also where in the stack — compile-time kernel selection or runtime routing?
maria: repro is small, pushing gist in a sec. appears at >512 seq lengths with kv-cache warm. the fused path applies rope before bias add (intentional for kernel speed) while legacy does bias then rope.
dina: oof ordering diffs are classic. did we verify the math is equivalent algebraically? rope(A + b) != rope(A) + rope(b) if rope is multiplicative position embedding (wrap/scale).
ryan: correct — rotary is multiplicative on queries/keys; bias is additive on q/k pre-attn. The algebra only commutes if bias is broadcasted to same dim and rope is linear — but implementations vary.
benchmark-bot: run summary — canary 0.3.4: 1200 inferences, mean ΔL2=0.0012, 73/200 eval prompts changed top-token.
maria: here's the gist: ```python
# simplified
q = Wq(x)
k = Wk(x) + bias
q = apply_rope(q)
k = apply_rope(k)
# fused path does apply_rope(Wq(x) + bias_q) in-kernel to avoid extra op
```
kevin: if fused kernel folds bias into the matmul output before rope, that will produce the different ordering. we did this to reduce kernel launches.
simran: can we make the fused kernel expose a flag to select order? e.g. `rope_after_bias: true|false` so we can gate via model profile.
aj: adding binary flags in kernels is awkward for JIT and perf testing, but feasible. downside: expands kernel variants combinatorially (rope/bias/dropout).
dina: also consider numeric stability — folding bias into matmul could change fp16 rounding and accumulation order, so even with algebraic equivalence you might see noise.
eva: what about adding a lightweight normalization test in the rollout: run N=50 deterministic prompts with seeds and check L2 < threshold and top-token match >= 99% before promoting?
ymaria: +1 to deterministic harness. my concern is failing evals that matter for customers (safety/regressions).
ryan: also remember dropout-free inference path removes stochastic masking but may change scaling if training used inverted dropout. Are we sure the inference path rescales appropriately?
kevin: good catch — our dropout-free path skips zeroing intermediate tensors but still applies the keep-scale when quantizing, but maybe we missed a multiply factor in combined-fused kernels.
natalia: (ops-bot) deployment note: canary 0.3.4 rolled back to 0.3.2 in us-west-2 at 10:12 UTC per rule due to metric threshold. :rotating_light:
simran: proposal: two-pronged approach — (1) quick patch: add an opt-in runtime flag `compat_mode=true` that forces legacy op ordering for canaries; (2) longer-term: canonicalize op order in fusion RFC and update kernels with doc + tests.
aj: agree. quick patch can be a runtime router policy so customers opt for strict determinism. will add a config: ```yaml
runtime:
  fused_qkv: auto
  fused_qkv_compat_mode: true  # force legacy ordering
  dropout_inference: disabled
  rope_bias_fusion: prefer_fused
```
dina: we should also add unit tests that assert commutation boundaries. e.g., numeric test with `seed=42` and `fp16` accum, compare fused vs legacy within epsilon.
ryan: I'll add a telemetry tag `fusion.ordering=legacy|fused` and sample traces for any top-token flips. Ops can auto-roll back if regression rate > 0.5%.
eva: for the rollout plan: start with 5% traffic on compat_mode=false in staging; run 10k prompts; if token-flip rate < 0.2% and ΔL2 < 5e-4 promote.
maria: also add a note to model-onboarding doc: require authors to declare whether models rely on bias order or rope ordering in their recipe.
kevin: ok. action items: @aj add runtime flag and router policy; @ryan add telemetry tag and gating alarms; @dina add unit tests + small fuzz harness; @simran coordinate canary. I'll draft the RFC appendix for kernel variants.
aj: will open PR for router + flag today, include microbench for perf delta. preliminary expect ~1.8% latency improvement when fused, but compatibility flag will cost an extra kernel launch.
simran: thanks — ping me when PR ready and I'll wire the canary config. :thumbsup:
benchmark-bot: perf note — folded-bias kernel vs legacy: median latency -1.8%, p50 -1.6%, p99 +0.4% (due to extra scheduling).
maria: thanks all — sharing the short repro in #eng-runtime once I scrub sensitive bits. want this tracked in the fusion follow-up RFC thread.
ryan: 👍
ops-bot: reminder — file an incident if regression affects >1% of production requests for more than 15 minutes.
kevin: closing loop: we'll prefer fused by default but keep compat flag until kernels stabilize. documenting tradeoffs in RFC follow-up.
eva: sounds good. I'll update the rollout checklist.
